name: Aurora
summary: Mature neighbourhoods, schools and quiet streets with fast commuter access.

hero.title: Living in Aurora
hero.subtitle: A NorthSide GTA community with strong schools, established neighbourhoods, and convenient access to Toronto.

snapshot.goTrainTime: Approx 50–55 minutes to Union Station from Aurora GO
snapshot.homePriceRange: Detached homes often trade in the mid-to-high $1M range, with townhomes providing more entry options.
snapshot.highways: Easy access to Highway 404 with connections toward Highway 400 via nearby routes.
snapshot.transitSummary: Aurora GO and local YRT/Viva routes connect to Toronto and neighbouring towns.

ratingDescriptions.housePrices: Aurora’s established detached homes keep pricing on the higher side for the NorthSide GTA.
ratingDescriptions.commuterAccess: Direct Highway 404 access and frequent GO trains make downtown commutes manageable.
ratingDescriptions.localTraffic: Local roads move steadily, though Yonge Street and Bayview can back up during rush hour.
ratingDescriptions.golf: Magna Golf Club, St. Andrew’s Valley, and nearby courses provide plenty of fairways.
ratingDescriptions.fishing: In-town fishing spots are limited, but Lake Simcoe and the Holland River are a quick drive away.
ratingDescriptions.trailsNature: The Aurora Arboretum, Sheppard’s Bush, and Moraine trails weave green space throughout town.
ratingDescriptions.restaurants: Independent restaurants downtown mix with convenient chains along Bayview and Wellington.
ratingDescriptions.localEvents: Seasonal farmers’ markets, concerts in the park, and community festivals keep the calendar full.

lifestyleHighlights.title: Nature & Green Space
lifestyleHighlights.description: Aurora sits along the Oak Ridges Moraine with trails, parks, and conservation areas linking neighbourhoods to the outdoors.

lifestyleHighlights.title: Community & Family Life
lifestyleHighlights.description: Established schools, recreation centres, and active minor sports make it easy for families to plug into the community.

lifestyleHighlights.title: Local Spots & Convenience
lifestyleHighlights.description: Downtown boutiques, big-box conveniences, and growing dining options keep errands and evenings close to home.

audiences.title: Families with Kids
audiences.description: Top-ranked public schools plus St. Andrew’s College and St. Anne’s School anchor education options.

audiences.title: Commuters & Professionals
audiences.description: Highway 404 and regular GO service keep downtown Toronto commutes practical on weekdays.

audiences.title: Active Lifestyles
audiences.description: Community centres, club sports, and nearby golf courses keep weekends busy.

audiences.title: Upsizers & Move-Up Buyers
audiences.description: Larger lots and mature trees provide space for upsizing without leaving the GTA.

neighbourhoods.name: Aurora Village
neighbourhoods.description: Historic downtown streets with century homes, cafés, and quick GO Station access.

neighbourhoods.name: Bayview Wellington
neighbourhoods.description: Family-friendly master-planned area with parks, schools, and everyday amenities.

neighbourhoods.name: Aurora Highlands
neighbourhoods.description: Tree-lined streets of detached homes close to top schools and the town’s recreation complex.

faqs.question: How long is the commute to Toronto?
faqs.answer: Highway 404 typically delivers a 40–50 minute drive to downtown Toronto, and GO trains run about 50–55 minutes to Union Station.

faqs.question: What types of homes are common here?
faqs.answer: Aurora is dominated by detached homes and townhomes from the 1980s onward, with some newer infill and estate properties.

faqs.question: Is Aurora good for families?
faqs.answer: Yes—Aurora is known for its school network, community programs, and recreation facilities that cater to families year-round.

faqs.question: What’s the general price point for homes?
faqs.answer: Detached homes often sell in the mid-to-high $1M range, with townhomes and semis offering slightly more attainable options.
